transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Anderson, thank you for coming in. I asked to meet with you because I have some difficult news regarding your son's developmental screening process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I appreciate you seeing me. I have been wondering why we hadn't heard back about the final evaluations.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: While reviewing the charts, I discovered a serious error. When your family declined that first appointment last year, the referral was marked as completed in our system. Because of that, no further follow-up was attempted and the screening didn't happen.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I remember we declined that specific date because of a family emergency. I assumed the system would trigger another invite or that someone would call.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It should have. I am very sorry. The responsibility for ensuring that follow-up happened lies with me and my team, and we failed to do that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is quite a shock. My son is already showing delays, and I feel like we have lost a critical window for intervention.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can hear how frustrating and devastating this is for you, especially knowing how much of a difference early intervention makes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Devastating is correct. I work in hospital administration, so I know how these things happen, but that doesn't make it acceptable. What does this actually mean for his prognosis? Is the damage permanent?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is difficult to give a definitive answer right now. Because we missed those months, we are starting the diagnostic process later than we should have. This may mean the trajectory of his progress will be slower than if we had caught this a year ago.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you're saying his long-term outlook has changed because of a clerical error?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a possibility. While we can't undo the lost time, we are focused on moving forward now. Does that explanation make sense, or can I clarify any part of how the error occurred?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: The explanation is clear. The impact is what concerns me. I want to know exactly what we are doing to fix this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, and—

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I also want to know who is auditing this. If a referral is simply closed because one appointment was declined, how many other children are falling through the cracks?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand you're concerned about the systemic failure. However, regarding your son, I think we should—

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am talking about my son. This is his life. I need to know if he can still reach his milestones or if we are looking at a permanent deficit.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will certainly find out as soon as we get the current assessments done. Now, about the next steps—

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like you're rushing me. I am asking you a direct question about my son's future.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not trying to rush, but we have a very tight schedule today and I need to get to my next clinic. Let's wrap up the emotional side and look at the logistics.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I find that remarkably cold. You've just told me my son's prognosis has been compromised and you're worried about your clinic schedule.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I apologize if that came across as cold. I genuinely care about the outcome here.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Then tell me the plan. What is the immediate next step?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll get the referrals sent out again. You'll probably get an email or a call from the specialists soon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Soon is not a timeline. Which specialists? When exactly will they call?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't give you an exact date because it depends on their scheduling, but just stay tuned for an email.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is completely inadequate. I expect a coordinated plan given the circumstances. Who is the point of contact for the follow-up?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The department will handle it. We'll see how it progresses.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are giving me nothing to hold onto here. I want a written timeline of the revised screening process by the end of the week.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll see what I can do.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't want you to see what you can do. I want a commitment.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll make a note of it. But as I mentioned, I really have to go now.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('tight schedule', 'wrap up the emotional side', 'really have to go now') and interrupts the patient's concerns.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the second turn using lay language and the resident checked for comprehension once ('Does that explanation make sense').

A.justification: Resident used direct apology language and explicitly took responsibility ('The responsibility... lies with me and my team') and maintained this accountability under pushback.

R.justification: Resident named specific emotions ('frustrating and devastating') and engaged with the patient's distress early in the conversation.

T.justification: The resident provided only placeholders ('stay tuned', 'we'll see how it progresses') and failed to provide a timeline or a coordinated plan.
